body:
Thanks for your significant effort before making an issue @SyedA5688.

Can you share which plate and which cell line you are testing? I want to first double check with our processed version of the data. 

Some potential issues: 1) the normalization should be done without a target sum, e.g. to the median of the data using `scanpy.pp.normalize_total`, and 2) the Tahoe data was not log transformed due to very low UMIs per cell.

Another potential issue: can you share the exact commands you used? The model expects only control cells for inference, so if your input anndata contains perturbed cells, that might also be the cause.

Thank you for your fast response!
I am testing on plate 1, cell line CVCL_0023. 

I checked again running inference on processed data following 1) normalization without a target sum and 2) non-log transformed data. At inference, I only inputed control cell expression with the labels for perturbations to apply to the control cells. The performance was still low however, with a pearson delta of around 0.05, which is lower than expected.

For inference, I used the cell-eval package to compute metrics between two AnnData objects: 1) the ground truth perturbed cell expression, and 2) the predictions of the Tahoe-ST model with control cells added (there was an error if control cells were not added to the expression predicted by Tahoe-ST). Here is the code for the inference call:
```
evaluator = MetricsEvaluator(
    adata_pred=model_pred_adata_with_controls,
    adata_real=gt_adata,
    control_pert="[('DMSO_TF', 0.0, 'uM')]",
    pert_col="drugname_drugconc",
    num_threads=64,
)
(results, agg_results) = evaluator.compute()
```

Hey @SyedA5688, looping in @yhr91 here. I think the checkpoint on hugging face might be the root cause. We have uploaded a new checkpoint.

Can you try redownloading it? Then, can you run the inference command as follows:

```
uv tool run --from git+ssh://github.com/ArcInstitute/state@0.9.1 state tx infer --model_dir ST-Tahoe --checkpoint ST-Tahoe/final.ckpt --pert_col drugname_drugconc --adata HOP62_control_template.h5ad --output HOP62_pred.h5ad
```

with this exact version and checkpoint, I was able to get much higher numbers. 

Thanks so much for your patience.

Thank you for updating the model! I have updated to the new Tahoe-ST model checkpoint locally, and redid inference on Tahoe data (processed as in my previous comment) using the inference command you posted. I still get numbers which I believe aren't representative of the model's performance on Tahoe data: I am wondering if something else could be off, either with my code version (I pulled the state GitHub repo at version 0.9.3) or my input control cell expression data for Tahoe-100M. Are there any plans to release the input data used in the STATE preprint, so that I may check my preprocessing against it? Thank you in advance!

Thanks again for your help here. I will update the thread here as we continue to debug and add utilities and data on our end.

My strong suspicion is that this is a data mismatch. Could you please share where you downloaded the Tahoe-100M data? Was it the arc virtual cell atlas? For the preprint, we used an early access version of the data that we plan to publish to HuggingFace this week - only issue is the file sizes, which we are actively working with them on.

Lastly, as you mention, it could be an issue with control cell expression. We will add this as a command line utility this week. For now, this is the command I used to paste in the control cell expression:

```
import anndata as ad
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Read the data
x = ad.read_h5ad('/large_storage/ctc/userspace/aadduri/preprint/tahoe_scaling_cs256/cs256/eval_last.ckpt/HOP62_real.h5ad')

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Identify control cells
control_condition = "[('DMSO_TF', 0.0, 'uM')]"
control_mask = x.obs['drugname_drugconc'] == control_condition
control_indices = np.where(control_mask)[0]

print(f"Found {len(control_indices)} control cells")

# Create a copy of the original data to modify
x_modified = x.copy()

# Get all unique perturbations (non-control)
unique_perturbations = x.obs['drugname_drugconc'].cat.categories
non_control_perturbations = [p for p in unique_perturbations if p != control_condition]

print(f"Processing {len(non_control_perturbations)} perturbations...")

# For each non-control perturbation, replace with randomly sampled control cells
for i, perturbation in enumerate(non_control_perturbations):
    # Find cells with this perturbation
    pert_mask = x.obs['drugname_drugconc'] == perturbation
    pert_indices = np.where(pert_mask)[0]
    n_pert_cells = len(pert_indices)

    if n_pert_cells > 0:
        # Sample n_pert_cells control cells randomly (with replacement)
        sampled_control_indices = np.random.choice(control_indices, size=n_pert_cells, replace=True)

        # Replace the expression data
        x_modified.X[pert_indices] = x.X[sampled_control_indices]

        # Print progress for every 50 perturbations
        if (i + 1) % 50 == 0:
            print(f"Processed {i + 1}/{len(non_control_perturbations)} perturbations")

print("Replacement complete!")
x_modified.write_h5ad('control_template.h5ad')
```

On the latest version (0.9.8), the inference script assumes the data is located in the .X of the adata by default. This is adjustable with the --embed-key parameter.

The processing I used for replacing control cell expression into the input AnnData objects seems similar to the code you pasted above, but it is greatly appreciated to have the exact code snippet. 3. I went ahead and did a pull of the latest code (version 0.9.8) and reran inference using the new Tahoe-ST Huggingface model as of July 14th. The results this time seemed much more realistic: It seems like [pull request 139](https://github.com/ArcInstitute/state/pull/139) fixed my issue with inference, and the performance (based on cell-eval) metrics looks much more closer to the preprint now. Thank you again for the assistance with troubleshooting, and looking forward to more updates to the GitHub repo.

Hello @SyedA5688 , I'm glad to see you've successfully reproduced the model results! I'm also very interested in the inference of ST model and have attempted to reproduce the reported evaluation results using data from the Tahoe-100M dataset. I've performed inference using the latest ST-Tahoe model (updated July 14th) and the latest code (version 0.9.8) , and evaluated the results with the cell-eval framework. However, there remains a significant gap between my evaluation metrics and the reported results. My evaluation metrics are as follows: My data processing pipeline follows a similar workflow to yours, though I'm unsure if there are minor differences between our approaches. I suspect the protein-coding gene filtering step might not have been implemented correctly, which could explain the significant performance gap. Below is my data processing code for your reference: ``` import anndata import os import scanpy as sc import pandas as pd import numpy as np # Filter protein-coding genes # return adata def filter_protein_coding_genes(adata): # Model parameters: 19,790 human protein-coding genes from SE model's protein_embeddings.pt file protein_coding_genes = pd.read_csv(r"D:\Projects\state\protein_gene.csv") # Model parameters: 2,000 highly variable genes (HVGs) from ST-Tahoe model's var_dims.pkl file hvg_names = pd.read_csv(r"D:\Projects\state\hvg_names.csv") # The 2,000 HVGs are not all from the 19,790 protein-coding genes, # and not all genes in the dataset are included in the 19,790 protein-coding genes. # There are 7 HVGs that are not in the 19,790 protein-coding genes, # these 7 genes are added to the protein-coding genes list for subsequent filtering. protein_coding_genes = pd.concat([protein_coding_genes, hvg_names[~hvg_names.key.isin(protein_coding_genes["key"])]], axis=0) protein_coding_mask = adata.var_names.isin(protein_coding_genes.key) # Filter adata genes based on the protein-coding gene mask return adata[:, protein_coding_mask] # Normalization, log transformation, and highly variable gene selection # hvg_names: whether to use the HVGs from model parameters (the HVGs used during model training) def normalize_log_hvg(adata, hvg_names=None): if "counts" not in adata.layers: adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy() sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4) sc.pp.log1p(adata) sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=2000, flavor="seurat_v3") if hvg_names is None: print("It is recommended to use the HVGs from the model, as the number of cells significantly affects HVG selection") # X_hvg = adata[:, adata.var['highly_variable']].X else: hvg_mask = adata.var_names.isin(hvg_names.key) X_hvg = adata[:, hvg_mask].X var_df = pd.DataFrame(index=hvg_names.key) X_adata = anndata.AnnData( X_hvg, obs = adata.obs, var = var_df ) return X_adata # Construct adata for inference def construct_infer_adata(adata, pert_col, control_pert, output_path, israndom=True): if control_pert == "DMSO_TF": control_pert = "[('DMSO_TF', 0.0, 'uM')]" DMSO_TF = adata[adata.obs[pert_col] == control_pert].copy() merged_adata = DMSO_TF.copy() # Record all perturbation labels present in the data for drugname_drugconc in adata.obs[pert_col].unique(): if drugname_drugconc == control_pert: continue tmp_adata = DMSO_TF.copy() if israndom: # Randomly sample the same number of cells from the control group as the perturbed group random_indices = np.random.choice(tmp_adata.n_obs, size=adata[adata.obs[pert_col] == drugname_drugconc].n_obs, replace=False) tmp_adata = tmp_adata[random_indices,:] # Copy the expression data from the control group (adata) and set the perturbation label (drugname_drugconc) # to the current perturbation label being processed tmp_adata.obs[pert_col] = drugname_drugconc # Concatenate all perturbed samples with the same perturbation label into one adata object merged_adata = anndata.concat([merged_adata, tmp_adata], axis=0, join="outer") merged_adata.obs.index.name = None # Temporarily remove index name merged_adata.write(output_path) merged_adata.obs.index.name = 'BARCODE_SUB_LIB_ID' # Restore index name (if needed) def main(): # Read adata # The read adata data was selected from the C32 cell line in the Tahoe-100M dataset, with approximately 200,000 cells randomly sampled, containing 94 perturbation labels. merged = sc.read(r"D:\Projects\state\input\merged.h5ad") hvg_names = pd.read_csv(r"D:\Projects\state\hvg_names.csv") adata = merged[merged.obs["plate"] == "plate4"] # Filter protein-coding genes adata = filter_protein_coding_genes(adata) # Normalization, log transformation, and highly variable gene selection # HVGs are selected based on the HVG names from model parameters adata = normalize_log_hvg(adata, hvg_names=hvg_names) pert_col = "drugname_drugconc" control_pert = "DMSO_TF" output_path = r"D:\Projects\state\input\infer_adata.h5ad" filt_adata = adata[adata.obs["drugname_drugconc"] == "[('DMSO_TF', 0.0, 'uM')]"].copy() num = 0 for drugname_drugconc in adata.obs[pert_col].unique(): if drugname_drugconc == "[('DMSO_TF', 0.0, 'uM')]": continue tmp_adata = adata[adata.obs["drugname_drugconc"] == drugname_drugconc].copy() filt_adata = anndata.concat([filt_adata, tmp_adata], axis=0, join="outer") num += 1 # if num == 20: # break # Save the original data for evaluation filt_adata.write(r"D:\Projects\state\input\real_adata.h5ad") # Construct adata for inference construct_infer_adata(filt_adata, pert_col, control_pert, output_path, israndom=True) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Any suggestions on potential preprocessing issues, particularly with protein-coding gene filtering?

Hi @xml12138,

Thanks for writing out your code snippet above. From what I can tell looking at the code, there are a few differences between your preprocessing and what ended up working for me:

1. In your normalize_log_hvg() function, you run Scanpy's normalize_total() function with target_sum=1e4. I took out the target sum, leaving it as the default value (None) so that it normalizes to the median of the data (mentioned by @abhinadduri  in an earlier comment). I also removed the log transformation, which appears to be in your function.
2. Regarding gene filtering, I filtered the raw Tahoe data to protein coding genes (similar to how you did above) using a list of protein coding genes that I curated myself (I could not find the standardized list). It is not the exact same protein coding gene list used by STATE, however I determined that it is close enough.

My exact preprocessing steps are:
1. Load raw Tahoe data
2. Filtering to 19.9k human protein coding genes
3. Normalize_total with no target_sum set
4. Filtering genes to the 2k highly variable genes given by the STATE model (in the var_dims pickle object in the Tahoe-ST model directory). I also had cases where some of the 2k HVGs were missing in the protein coding genes; in those cases (13 genes), I filled in zeros for those genes and added them to the gene features so that they would be in the final AnnData object).
5. Replacing control cell expression into AnnData for STATE input

Hope this helps!

Thank you so much for the detailed explanation！I've adjusted the preprocessing pipeline according to your suggestions and successfully reproduced results that closely match the reported outputs. Here are the specific changes I made: 1. Switched to default parameters for normalization (i.e., median-based scaling instead of fixed target_sum=1e4); 2. Removed the log transformation step (also appreciated the earlier reminder from @abhinadduri about this). Additionally, your note about "zero-filling missing HVGs" in the preprocessing details was particularly enlightening—it helped me gain a deeper understanding of STATE model's input requirements. Thanks again for your patient guidance！
